rules: Do not raise RC9's minimum iOS version above 16.0.
Preserve all iOS 16.x firmware/device combinations supported by RC9's existing 3.0.7 RootHide jailbreak paths, not only the user's iPadOS 16.5 device.
Maintain an explicit iOS 16.x firmware, device/chip, exploit, and offset matrix; distinguish source-derived support from device-validated combinations.
Do not infer jailbreak support for every iOS 16.x release or device from the app's MinimumOSVersion of 16.0.
Only port upstream behavior that is available and correct on iOS 16.
Exclude behavior requiring iOS 17 or later; when a newer API is optional, require an iOS 16 fallback and an explicit availability guard.
Review every upstream API and ABI change against iOS 16 before implementation.
validation: Both app Debug and Release deployment targets remain 16.0.
The full RC9 iOS 16.x version/device/exploit/offset support matrix is inventoried and validation evidence is tracked per combination.
Device acceptance is recorded on the user's iOS 16 hardware separately from CI.

backports.limits: No proof of all inherited-descriptor lifetimes, post-fork configuration locks, or iOS device behavior.

backports.scope: Tri-state adhoc collection, parse/hash failure propagation, checked growth and partial-output cleanup.

backports.limits: Not the full upstream trustcache_fs walker, signature attachment, randomization rollback, parser-submodule, or kernel trustcache lifecycle audit.

phase_four.scope: Propagate directory open/read/stat/allocation/parse/callback/close failures, reject partial collections, probe Mach-O magic with EINTR and short-read handling, and clean up all add-entrypoint outcomes.
preserved: File collector path filtering and per-slice randomization.
Recursive toggle and no symlink or special-file traversal.

phase_five.scope: Default injection mode, optional manager installation and existing verbose-log switch audit.
phase_five.preserved: Existing whitelist file and user choices are not deleted, rewritten or forcibly disabled.
phase_five.unresolved: No group-member device evidence establishes which component created their user whitelist file. The optional Sileo entry was absent at this phase's baseline; phase_eleven adds it without changing injection mode.

phase_six.scope: Injection policy cache snapshots, concurrent readers and fork child state.
changes: Publish a fresh per-process cache state after fork without touching an inherited lock or XPC snapshot.
Read each config through one descriptor and verify device, inode, type, size, mtime and ctime remain stable.
Retry interrupted reads and avoid publishing short or concurrently modified file contents.
Preserve the prior valid snapshot during invalid or transient reads; clear it when the path is removed or is no longer a regular file.
preserved: Per-call-site cache structure rather than ZQBB's global LRU.
Injection mode selector, blacklist/whitelist precedence and config keys.
RC9 iOS 16 deployment target, UI, low-power and custom-mount features.

native_harness_cases: same-size content change with restored mtime
invalid intermediate content preserves previous valid snapshot
fork child reads while inherited parent cache lock is held

limitations: Host XPC parser and unfair lock are test doubles.
No iOS arm64/arm64e device acceptance yet.
vfork semantics, all post-fork lock lifetimes and repeated-fork child memory lifetime remain under review.
A persistently invalid config keeps the last valid policy until a valid update or path removal.

findings.evidence: RC9's gJbTrustcacheLock serializes its append/clear operations but not trustcache_file_upload or kernel readers. Same-size updates write in place; size changes unlink and free after a fixed 10ms delay. The fixed official and ZQBB references share this pattern.
findings.required_before_fix: Prove kernel reader synchronization and allocation reclamation semantics; a user-space mutex or longer sleep is not sufficient.

findings.evidence: RC9 rolls back synchronous move failures, but no startup journal restores dyld if execution stops after patched dyld moves to dyld.old and before inflight dyld publishes at dyld.
findings.fallback: On the next explicit app jailbreak, prepareBootstrap republishes the app-bundled basebin before loadBasebinTrustcache; later jailbreak steps regenerate patched dyld. This is a user-triggered whole-bundle reset, not automatic journal recovery, and can roll back a live update to the bundled version.
findings.test_gap: Current dyld tests inject returned filesystem errors, not process termination and restart between each publish operation.

findings.evidence: jbupdate_basebin validates a staged payload but replaces live top-level entries by remove-then-copy. Version markers are process environment only; no durable per-item backup/journal restores a partial batch.
findings.distinct_from: DOBootstrapper stage/ready/backup is not the live updater's automatic journal or rollback. On the next explicit app jailbreak, it republishes the app-bundled basebin before trustcache load, providing a user-triggered whole-bundle reset that may roll back a live update.
findings.test_gap: Current updater tests inject synchronous remove/copy errors but do not assert rollback of earlier items or model termination mid-transaction.

required_closure: If automatic interruption recovery is required, design a durable, idempotent journal before changing runtime publication behavior; otherwise document the manual bundled-basebin reset and its rollback consequence.
Inject termination after every update mutation and verify the selected recovery path before launchd consumes basebin or dyld.
Preserve active dyld vnode, fakelib mount and RootHide path semantics.

phase_eight.scope: Generated-dyld helper API parity and the legacy Corellium standalone call path.

finding.evidence: Official and ZQBB expose basebin_generate_internal(originUsrLibPath, basebinPath, targetBasebinPath, ...); RC9's BaseBin/dopamine main retained that call while its header and implementation no longer exposed the symbol. The standard iOS app path uses basebin_generate and was not affected by this missing helper.
finding.change: Restore the parameterized helper and header declaration; keep RC9's checked filesystem operations and immediate move-error rollback; preserve basebin_generate as a wrapper using /usr/lib and the active jbroot basebin.
finding.test: tests/test_rc9_dyld.py source contract for declaration, definition, standalone caller and wrapper

limits: The public TIPA workflow does not compile the Corellium standalone target.
This API restoration does not close generated-dyld process-interruption recovery.
No product version, minimum iOS target or device support claim changed.

changes: Propagate kernel reads and writes through trustcache list traversal and mutation.
Conditionally roll back failed pointer writes; retain allocations when list publication state is uncertain.
Preserve RC9 locking, deduplication and cross-page behavior while checking dynamic cache bounds and I/O.
limits: The 10ms retirement delay is not proof that kernel trustcache readers have quiesced.
The fix targets the iOS 16 PPL trustcache path and shared list operations; no iOS 17-only strategy was ported.

phase_ten.scope: Guard signature re-encoding failure in trust_signatures without changing the successful attachment path.

finding.evidence: Both comparison paths dereference the result of csd_superblob_encode without checking it. RC9 additionally frees the original signature buffer before encoding, so an allocation failure could cause a null dereference and discard the original buffer.
finding.change: Encode to a temporary first; preserve the original allocation on failure, clean up local state and return the existing -2 allocation-failure status. Replace the original only after successful encoding.
finding.test: tests/test_rc9_signature_attachment.py extracts the production trust_signatures function and injects encode failure and success.

limits: The added guard is a local failure-path hardening, not an upstream backport.
It does not close remaining signature parser/attachment paths or trustcache kernel-reader lifetime.

phase_eleven.scope: Optional companion-tool Sileo links and ownership comparison for mount/trust preferences.
changes: Add jailbreak-only Sileo package-detail links for cn.zqbb.inject.manager and cn.zqbb.hello.mnt using existing DOButtonCell row heights.
Port the ZQBB sileoURLScheme method unchanged; read Sileo URL types from the active jbroot and fall back to sileo.
Keep the upstream open-failure message, use existing RC9 error/OK keys and explicitly dispatch alert presentation to the main queue.
preserved: Existing blacklist/whitelist selection and user configuration.
No automatic package installation, privilege change, new timer or daemon.
RC9 custom mount execution/persistence and independent manager trust preferences.
Existing iOS 16 deployment target, scrolling, bounce, glass rendering and menu hierarchy.
limits: Host native tests exercise the production Foundation scheme reader, not UIKit, Sileo routing or package installation.
External mount manager implementation and independent trust-manager behavior are not certified by adding package links.
This does not close full iOS 16 device coverage, trustcache reader lifetime or dyld/basebin interruption recovery.

phase_twelve.scope: Signature source positional reads and hash failure propagation.
changes: Use bounded positional reads without changing the shared file offset; retry EINTR and positive short reads, reject errors and incomplete reads.
Check negative file positions and subtraction-based file bounds before offset addition; reject null allocation sources.
Stop on code-directory hash failure before querying or publishing hashes; free temporary state and return the existing generic -1 failure.
limits: The raw-byte resolver test does not validate ChOma parser layouts or iOS kernel ABI.
Internal blob validation, concurrent file-mutation consistency and other skipped failure branches remain open.
No UI, version, iOS support scope, injection defaults, low-power schedule or mount behavior changes.
